# peekme

> peekme explains text you select in a coding agent's terminal. It runs in front of Claude Code, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI and Kiro CLI. Select words in the agent's output and press Alt+P (Option+P on a Mac): a short explanation opens right under them, inside the terminal, and Esc puts the screen back exactly as it was. Alt+Shift+P asks your own question about the selection. Free and open source (MIT or Apache-2.0), written in Rust, for Linux and macOS, also inside tmux and over SSH.

Install: `npm i -g peekme && peekme install` (or `brew install gregorybolshakov/tap/peekme`, or `cargo install peekme`), then open a new terminal and start the agent as always. No API key: explanations go through the agent's own CLI and login. Unlike the agents' built-in side questions (Claude Code /btw, Codex /side, Copilot CLI /ask), you select the words instead of typing a question, the answer opens next to them, boxes can open inside boxes, and answers stay on the screen as clickable underlines.
